title: Expose CUDA Philox RNG state reservation to Python as Generator.philox_cuda_state
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.15.0) (oldest at bottom):
* #191020
* __->__ #191019

Python-authored CUDA kernels (e.g. the DSL overrides in torch/_native) need
to implement RNG ops that draw from the same Philox stream as aten's eager
kernels: reserve a chunk of the stream, get (seed, offset), advance the
generator. That primitive exists in C++ as
CUDAGeneratorImpl::philox_cuda_state(increment) but has no Python exposure;
the closest is the inductor-private inductor_reserve_rng_state dispatcher op.

Generator.philox_cuda_state(increment) returns (seed, offset, intragraph)
as three 1-element int64 tensors; kernels consume (seed, offset +
intragraph). Tensors rather than ints so the same code is CUDA-graph-safe:
during capture, seed/offset alias the generator's per-capture extragraph
tensors, which replay_prologue refills on every replay — a kernel that loads
them at run time needs no capture-specific plumbing. The extragraph storage
is made non-resizable so a caller cannot reallocate it out from under a
captured graph. Reservation semantics (increment rounded up to a multiple
of 4, offset % 4 invariant) match every other philox_cuda_state caller.

The API is public and documented (torch/_torch_docs.py), including the
graph-capture aliasing/lifetime contract and the int64 reinterpretation of
the uint64 seed and offset.

Authored with Claude Code.

Test Plan:

New tests in test/test_cuda.py: eager reservation values and offset
advancement, increment rounding, reproducibility of a reservation via
set_offset, seed/offset int64-reinterpretation at >= 2**63, error cases,
shared graphsafe state, and graph capture/replay including non-resizability
of the returned aliases.

```
python test/test_cuda.py -k philox_cuda_state -v
python test/test_cuda.py -k graphsafe -v
```

cc @albanD
